name: notepadia-theia-upgrade-procedure
purpose: A deterministic, prompt-executable procedure for moving Notepadia from one Eclipse Theia release line to a newer one. It is written to be handed to an agent: every step names the exact files, commands, and gates, and it assumes no knowledge beyond this repository. Run it whole; do not skip gates.
whenToRun: A new stable Eclipse Theia release exists and is newer than the pinned baseline.
A Theia security fix or Electron/runtime compatibility fix is required.
The upstream @theia/monaco-editor-core Monaco version moves and the editor integration must be re-validated.
NOT for: adding a Theia package that was not already in use (treat that as a feature, not an upgrade), or a Notepadia-only change.

baseline.runtime: browser (http://localhost:3000) is the shipping target; Electron is packaging

inputs.targetTheiaVersion: Required. Exact version string, e.g. "1.76.0". No ranges, no caret/tilde.
inputs.reason: Required. One line: why the upgrade is being taken.
inputs.electronTargetVersion: Optional. Only if the upgrade forces an Electron bump; otherwise keep 42.10.0.
inputs.runElectronPackaging: Optional boolean, default false. Whether to also produce installers in this procedure.
inputs.allowBreakingChanges: Optional boolean, default false. Must be explicitly true to accept a compile break that requires product code changes.

manifestTouchPoints.role: single lockfile for the whole workspace; regenerate via yarn, never hand-edit

fragileIntegrationPoints.why: Imports internal, non-public Monaco ESM paths ('@theia/monaco-editor-core/esm/vs/editor/standalone/browser/standaloneServices', '/esm/vs/platform/keybinding/common/keybinding') and StandaloneKeybindingService. These paths are unversioned internals and are the most likely thing to move.
fragileIntegrationPoints.watch: Does the module still export StandaloneServices/StandaloneKeybindingService at the same path? Do editor chunks still resolve?

fragileIntegrationPoints.why: Overrides Monaco's find widget handler and depends on monaco.editor.FindMatch, ICodeEditor.getOption(wordSeparators), EditorOption names, and model.findMatches signature.
fragileIntegrationPoints.watch: monaco.editor.EditorOption.wordSeparators, findMatches arg list, ICodeEditor option APIs.

fragileIntegrationPoints.why: Central command/menu registration against @theia/core menu ids and CommandRegistry.
Uses StatusBar API (addElement/removeElement) whose surface has changed across Theia releases.
Editor/widget option wiring (renderWhitespace, glyphMargin, etc.) and preference names.
Electron main module, updater (electron-updater), and IPC bootstrap must match @theia/electron expectations.
Build pipeline glue; Theia has changed whether webpack or esbuild is the supported path.

phase0_preflight.goal: Start from a known-clean, builds-green baseline so a later failure is attributable.

steps.action: Confirm a clean tree.
Record the current green baseline.
Verify the toolchain matches the baseline.
steps.expect: node 24.x, yarn 1.x, no missing native deps

steps.action: Confirm the baseline builds and tests pass BEFORE any change.
steps.expect: build succeeds; all extension tests pass

phase1_discover.goal: Choose a target version that is real, stable, and internally consistent.

steps.action: Read the target version's npm dist-tags and the GitHub release notes for @theia/cli.
steps.expect: target version exists as 'latest' or an explicit stable tag

steps.action: Confirm every package in allTheiaPackages publishes the SAME target version (Theia is released in lock-step).
steps.command: npm view <pkg>@<target> version for each pkg
steps.expect: all equal; if any is missing, STOP - do not mix release lines

steps.action: Read the release notes/CHANGELOG for the target and every version in between. Capture every 'breaking', 'removed API', 'Monaco', 'Electron', and 'engines' note into the upgrade report.
steps.expect: a written list of breaking changes

steps.action: Check the target's Node engines requirement and its @theia/monaco-editor-core (Monaco) version.
steps.expect: node requirement is satisfied by 24.x; note the Monaco version delta

steps.action: Re-check the highest-risk item: do the internal Monaco paths in fragileIntegrationPoints still exist in the target?
steps.command: inspect node_modules/@theia/monaco-editor-core after install, or the @theia/monaco source for the target
steps.expect: either the paths exist, or plan the P4 fix now

steps.action: Create a branch named for the target.

phase3_bump.goal: Move every Theia pin to exactly the target, in one commit.

steps.action: In applications/browser/package.json, set @theia/* deps and devDep @theia/cli to the exact target version. Keep any @theia package OUT if it was not already present.
In applications/electron/package.json, set @theia/* deps INCLUDING @theia/electron, and devDep @theia/cli, to the target.
In extensions/notepadia/package.json, set its @theia/* dependencies to the target. Do NOT add @theia/cli here.
Only if P1.4 requires it, bump Electron/electron-builder in applications/electron. Otherwise leave them.
Sweep for any straggler @theia pins at the old version.
steps.expect: every hit reads the target version

phase4_install_rebuild.goal: Reproduce the dependency tree and native/prebuild artifacts.

steps.action: Install with the repo's lockfile conventions (do not change .yarnrc).
steps.expect: lockfile updated to the target; no peer-dep failure

steps.action: Rebuild browser prebuilds.
Rebuild electron prebuilds (desktop).
If a native module refuses to rebuild, clean and reinstall before debugging anything else.

phase5_build.goal: Compile all TypeScript and bundle all targets.

steps.action: Build the extension first - it fails fastest and pinpoints API moves.
Build the browser app.
Build the electron app.

If P5.x fails, classify each error before touching code: (a) moved/renamed public API, (b) moved internal Monaco path, (c) Node/engines mismatch, (d) genuine product regression. Do not paper over (d).

phase6_fix.goal: Repair only what the upgrade actually broke, at the smallest correct scope.

steps.action: Fix public-API moves by following the release notes' replacement. Keep behavior identical unless allowBreakingChanges is true.

Fix moved internal Monaco paths in notepadia-editor-keybinding-contribution.ts (and anywhere else) against the installed @theia/monaco-editor-core. Prefer a public seam if one exists; if none exists, isolate the internal import behind a single small module so the next upgrade touches one file.
Re-run Phase 5 until all three builds are green.
Do not silently drop a Notepad++ behavior to make a build pass; if a behavior cannot survive the upgrade, record it as an explicit finding and stop for a decision when allowBreakingChanges is false.

phase7_test.goal: Prove the upgrade on the same gates the project already trusts.

steps.action: Unit tests (extension).
steps.expect: all pass; the pure-logic contract is unchanged unless intentionally changed

steps.action: Lint.
Preference-default guard.
Browser smoke.
End-to-end.
Electron smoke (when desktop is in scope).

phase8_manual_acceptance.goal: The automated suites do not cover the Notepad++ surface; a human-or-agent pass must.

steps.action: Start the browser app.
Walk the acceptanceCriteria list below at http://localhost:3000.

Specifically re-test the fragileIntegrationPoints: Ctrl+F / Ctrl+H open the Notepadia dialog (not Monaco's widget); Find Next/Prev, regex, whole-word, selection-only; the File/Edit/View menus and their keybindings; status bar fields; word wrap; zoom chords.
Set the build version.
Package per platform.
steps.command: yarn package:win | yarn package:linux | yarn package:mac

steps.action: Launch the packaged app once and confirm it reaches the workbench and opens a file.

phase10_document.goal: Leave the repo self-describing at the new baseline.

steps.action: Update the baseline in prompt/notepadia-generation-prompt.json and prompt/pair_programming_prompt_v8.1.0.json (or its successor) to the target version.
Update README.md and docs/*.md where the Theia version or build pipeline is stated.
Add a CHANGELOG.md entry recording from-version, to-version, breaking changes handled, and anything intentionally deferred.
Produce the upgrade report (see deliverables).
Stage only the upgrade files; inspect the diff.
Commit with a conventional message.
Open a PR whose description contains the upgrade report from Phase 10 / deliverables.

acceptanceCriteria: Every @theia package across all three manifests reads the same exact target version; no caret/tilde remains on any @theia entry.
yarn build:extensions, yarn build:browser, and yarn build:electron all succeed from a clean checkout.
yarn test, yarn lint, yarn check:prefs, yarn smoke, and yarn test:e2e all pass.
Ctrl+F and Ctrl+H open the Notepadia Find dialog, not Monaco's inline widget.
Find Next / Find Previous / regex / match-case / whole-word / wrap-around / selection-only behave as before.
The Notepad++ menu bar, toolbar, tab bar, and status bar render and respond as before.
Opening, editing, saving, and closing a real file round-trips; no Monaco option regressions (tab size, insert spaces, word wrap, whitespace rendering).
No new console errors or unhandled promise rejections on startup.
The recorded baseline versions in the prompt JSON files and docs match the target.

rollback.trigger: A gate fails and the fix is not small and safe.
steps: git switch -c the original branch and discard the upgrade branch, OR reset the three manifests and yarn.lock to the recordedRef and re-run yarn install.
yarn --cwd applications/browser rebuild && yarn --cwd applications/electron rebuild
yarn build && yarn test to confirm the baseline is green again.
rollback.note: Prefer reverting the whole upgrade commit over partially reverting individual Theia packages; mixing release lines is the one state that must never be committed.

guardrails: Never mix @theia package versions across release lines, even temporarily.
Never hand-edit yarn.lock; change manifests and run yarn.
Never introduce a standalone monaco-editor dependency; use Theia's Monaco integration only.
Do not add webpack if the target uses the esbuild pipeline; do not remove esbuild if it does.
Keep product-specific behavior in extensions/notepadia; do not fork @theia source into the repo.
Do not claim success without a green build and the test gates above.
If allowBreakingChanges is false, any required product-code behavior change is a STOP-and-ask, not a fix.
Preserve .yarnrc, the lockfile, and Yarn Classic conventions.
deliverables: The three updated manifests and the regenerated yarn.lock.
Any product-code fixes required by the upgrade, each minimal and explained.
An upgrade report (JSON or Markdown) with: from/to versions, the breaking-changes list from P1.3, per-error classification from P5.4, the exact commands run and their outcomes, and anything deferred.
Updated docs and prompt baselines at the new version.
One conventional-commit commit and a PR description carrying the report.
outOfScope: Adding Theia features that were not already present.
Refactoring Notepadia code unrelated to the upgrade.
Changing the product version/calver unless packaging is in scope.
Bumping React, ESLint, TypeScript, or other non-Theia dependencies unless the upgrade strictly requires it.
notesForTheAgent: Treat the fragileIntegrationPoints list as the primary risk register: re-verify each item explicitly and say so in the report.
The browser target is the shipping product; if time is short, validate browser fully and note electron as unverified rather than implying it passed.
When an internal Monaco path moves, wrap it in one small adapter module so the next upgrade is a one-file change.
Keep each phase's evidence (command output) to paste into the report; a gate with no evidence is not passed.
